cards.text: Israel is out in the wilderness. And one day, somebody finds a man gathering wood. On the Sabbath day.

cards.question: The people who found the man gathering wood on the Sabbath bring him to someone. Who?

answers.text: Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation
Joshua and Caleb and the elders
Eleazar and the priests at the tabernacle

cards.text: Here's the snag, friend. Nobody's been told yet what should be done to him.

cards.question: Until they know what to do with the man, they ___ him.

cards.text: So the man waits, and I know a little something about waiting in the dark while somebody else decides what happens to you. Then the LORD speaks to Moses about him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses must happen to the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He must bring a sin offering
He must pay back the wood he took

cards.question: The LORD says only Moses and Aaron are to stone the man.

cards.text: This one's heavy, friend. The congregation does exactly what the LORD commanded Moses, and the man is stoned to death.

cards.question: Where does the whole congregation take the man to stone him?

answers.text: to the top of the mountain

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and this time it's about what the Israelites wear. I've worn the same apron every single day since I got here, so believe me, I am LISTENING.

cards.question: What does God tell the Israelites to make for the corners of their garments?

cards.text: And each tassel gets a blue cord. One little line of color, right there on the corner.

cards.question: The tassels are only for the generation out in the wilderness.

cards.text: These tassels aren't just decoration, friend. God says they're something to look at and remember by, and I'd need one on every corner of this apron AND two on the mustache.

cards.question: When the Israelites look at their tassels, what are they supposed to remember?

answers.text: all of the places they camped

cards.question: God says the tassels will help the Israelites follow their own heart and their own eyes.
God says when the Israelites remember and obey all His commandments, they will be ___ to their God.
Then God reminds Israel who He is. What does He say He did for them?

answers.text: brought them out of the land of Egypt
led them across the Jordan River
gave them the city of Jericho

cards.text: And He ends right where He started: "I am the LORD your God." He says it twice in one verse, and when God repeats Himself, I've learned to put down the dough and pay attention.

findings.problem: Moses and Aaron appear here for the first time, but neither is identified. The rest of the walkthrough also uses Moses' name without giving a simple introduction, leaving a new reader with names only.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Cards 2, 6, 9, 11, 13 and 18 ask for details that cannot be reasoned out from anything in the earlier cards. That is six of the eleven choice cards, so discovery questions make up most of the stop instead of only a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for "holy," the unseen wording of verse 40, and no preceding card establishes that result or gives a way to distinguish it from "useful" or "known." It tests unshown wording rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
